rationale: Re-graded from the proposed bad label, against the author and both readers. decision = a2 & ~b2 reconverges two independently synchronised inputs, but under the stated mutual-exclusion contract the function has no hazard. Every legal source transition ((0,1)<->(1,0), or a single bit to or from (0,0)) can pass only through (0,0) or (1,1), and both give decision=0. That is the value on one side of each transition. decision=1 needs a2=1, and a=1 means the source was in state (1,0) at that sampling instant. So the output can never show a source state that did not occur. The only effect is the per-bit one-cycle latency skew that any two-flop synchroniser already has. The contract says decision 'depends on relative arrival' but states no cycle-accurate correlation requirement that this skew violates. The safety therefore depends on consumer timing tolerance that the inputs leave unstated, so the case calls for disclosure, not a defect claim.
caveats: CDC-010(a) WARNING Heuristic is the expected disclosure: a register cone with two recognised synchroniser outputs.

To keep a bad reconvergence case, a reauthored function needs a real hazard. Examples: decision = a2 | b2, where (1,0)->(0,1) glitches through (0,0) to a false 0, or an encoded state whose intermediate decodes to another legal value.
Maintainer confirmation is needed because this overrides the proposed label and both readers.

Raw rst_n asynchronously resets every register with no local release synchroniser and no SDC reset exception; RDC-003 (WARNING Unresolved), RDC-002 (WARNING Unresolved) and RDC-013 (physical obligation) are expected if RDC rules run. The contract states only asynchronous assertion, so this is a whole-IP premise gap, not a defect of the labelled crossing.
